diseases.name: Anthracnose
diseases.description: A fungal disease of mango that can affect leaves, flowers and fruit.
symptoms: Dark brown to black spots on leaves
Blossom blight and twig dieback in severe cases
precautions: Remove and dispose of heavily affected plant material away from the orchard
Improve airflow through appropriate pruning
Avoid unnecessary leaf wetness
Handle harvested fruit carefully to limit injury
next_steps: Consult a local agricultural extension officer or plant pathologist to confirm the cause.
Follow local agricultural guidance, product labels and regulations for any treatment.

diseases.name: Bacterial Canker
diseases.description: A bacterial disease that can cause angular leaf lesions and cankers.
symptoms: Angular, water-soaked leaf spots that turn dark
Raised lesions or cankers on twigs and fruit
conditions: Wet, windy weather and plant wounds can favour spread
precautions: Remove and dispose of infected tissue
Disinfect pruning tools between plants
Avoid working in the orchard when foliage is wet
next_steps: Consult a local agricultural extension officer or plant pathologist to confirm the cause.
Follow local agricultural guidance, product labels and regulations for any treatment.

diseases.name: Healthy appearance
diseases.description: The model found no visible signs matching the supported disease classes. This does not guarantee the plant is disease-free.
precautions: Continue regular orchard monitoring
Re-check if new spots, coatings or discolouration appear
next_steps: Take another photo if you still have concerns, or consult a local expert.

diseases.name: Powdery Mildew
diseases.description: A fungal disease that produces a whitish powdery growth on young tissue.
symptoms: White to grey powdery coating on leaves or flower panicles
precautions: Monitor flowering shoots closely
Improve airflow through appropriate pruning
Remove severely affected tissue
next_steps: Consult a local agricultural extension officer or plant pathologist to confirm the cause.
Follow local agricultural guidance, product labels and regulations for any treatment.

diseases.name: Scab
diseases.description: A fungal disease causing raised, corky or scabby lesions on young tissue.
symptoms: Small raised spots on leaves and shoots
Scab-like or corky patches on fruit
precautions: Remove affected shoots
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness where possible
Maintain orchard hygiene
next_steps: Consult a local agricultural extension officer or plant pathologist to confirm the cause.
Follow local agricultural guidance, product labels and regulations for any treatment.

diseases.name: Sooty Mould
diseases.description: A dark fungal growth on honeydew produced by sap-sucking insects. It is largely a surface coating.
symptoms: Black, soot-like film on leaf surfaces
precautions: Inspect for the insects that produce honeydew
Address the insect problem, since the mould follows it
Gentle cleaning of affected surfaces
next_steps: Consult a local agricultural extension officer or plant pathologist to confirm the cause.
Follow local agricultural guidance, product labels and regulations for any treatment.

diseases.name: Stem End Rot
diseases.description: A fungal disease associated with decay starting at the stem end, commonly seen after harvest.
symptoms: Dark, spreading decay near the stem end
conditions: Plant stress, wounds and warm, humid storage
precautions: Handle fruit gently and avoid injuries
Remove dead wood and affected material
Store and transport fruit under clean, well-ventilated conditions
next_steps: Consult a local agricultural extension officer or plant pathologist to confirm the cause.
Follow local agricultural guidance, product labels and regulations for any treatment.
